picks.headline: GPT-5.6이 50년 묵은 그래프 이론 난제를 증명했다
picks.excerpt: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol produced a proof of the cycle double cover conjecture, a graph-theory problem open for more than 50 years. Mathematicians say the result shows AI tools are already changing how mathematical research gets done, not just how it gets checked.
picks.rationale: A machine-generated proof of a 50-year-old open conjecture is the highest-novelty AI-in-science result in the pool, and it shifts AI from proof-checker to proof-producer.

picks.headline: 확산 모델은 왜 베끼지 않고 새로 그리는가
picks.excerpt: Google Research offers a mathematical account of why diffusion models produce genuinely new images rather than copies: a 'score smoothing' effect that emerges from neural-network training. The models interpolate between training examples along a hidden data manifold instead of memorizing them.
picks.rationale: A first-party mathematical explanation of image-model originality — directly changes how designers reason about what a generative model is actually doing with training data.

picks.headline: 합성하기 전에 펩타이드 성질을 예측하는 오픈소스 AI
picks.excerpt: Penn Engineers released PeptiVerse, an open-source AI platform that forecasts the chemical and biological properties of peptides before anyone synthesizes them. Screening in silico first could cut the cost and time of developing peptide drugs such as weight-loss therapeutics.
picks.rationale: An actually-released open-source platform (not a paper promise) that lets labs screen peptide candidates in silico before synthesis — usable capability, not commentary.

picks.headline: 의료 AI는 생각보다 환자 정보를 훨씬 많이 흘린다
picks.excerpt: New work shows membership-inference attacks can pull sensitive patient information out of medical AI models far more effectively than the field assumed. The leakage is concentrated among underrepresented patient groups, meaning the privacy cost falls hardest on the people models already serve worst.
picks.rationale: A measured attack result that resets a safety assumption for anyone training models on sensitive data, with a sharp fairness twist — the leakage concentrates on underrepresented groups.

picks.headline: 호기심을 심은 로봇이 언어를 두 배 빨리 배웠다
picks.excerpt: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology researchers gave robots a curiosity-driven learning signal and found they picked up language roughly twice as fast as incurious counterparts. The robots spontaneously played and reproduced the same characteristic grammatical errors human toddlers make before recovering from them.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool (07-23) and a genuine capability result: an intrinsic-curiosity signal doubles language-learning speed while reproducing human developmental error patterns.
